channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: China’s $17 Billion Crop Pledge Falters Ahead of Trump-Xi Summit
item.description: China looks unlikely to fulfill a pledge to buy billions of dollars in US farm products in 2026 as the leaders of the two nations prepare for their third meeting this year.
item.dc:creator: Erin Ailworth, Hallie Gu and Michael Hirtzer

item.title: Defense Department Again Fails to Produce a Reliable Audit
item.description: The Pentagon once again failed to achieve a so-called clean audit of its vast operations, but pledged that Ernst & Young — awarded a five-year, $990 million contract — and artificial intelligence tools will help it make the grade in the fiscal 2028 review.
item.dc:creator: Tony Capaccio

item.title: United Airlines Says It Has a Widespread System Outage: AP
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Maryland Governor Wes Moore discusses his second-term priorities, including housing, immigration and the data center buildout. Kristy Kiernan, Associate Director of Embry-Riddle’s Boeing Center for Aviation and Aerospace Safety, discusses the fallout from Friday’s FAA outage, a separate United Airlines system outage, the risks of accelerating the agency’s technology overhaul and why travelers should still feel confident flying. Former Treasury Secretary Jack Lew discusses tensions between Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick over China policy, the administration’s handling of chip export controls and the fallout surrounding Nvidia. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Panama President Orders Formal Talks With First Quantum on Mine
item.description: Panama President Jose Raul Mulino ordered formal talks with First Quantum Minerals Ltd. to discuss reopening the firm’s idled copper mine in the country.
item.dc:creator: Michael McDonald

item.title: Lew: US Needs To Be ‘Clear and Consistent’ with China
item.description: Former Treasury Secretary Jack Lew discusses tensions between Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick over China policy, the administration’s handling of chip export controls and the fallout surrounding Nvidia. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Aviation Expert Warns Against FAA Upgrade Shortcuts
item.description: Kristy Kiernan, Associate Director of Embry-Riddle’s Boeing Center for Aviation and Aerospace Safety, discusses the fallout from Friday’s FAA outage, a separate United Airlines system outage, the risks of accelerating the agency’s technology overhaul and why travelers should still feel confident flying. She speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily Podcast: Global AI Chip Race
item.description:
The Trump administration moved to limit several countries from providing Chinese companies remote access to advanced artificial intelligence chips and servers, following increased scrutiny over its handling of curbs on semiconductor exports after an alleged espionage scandal involving Nvidia Corp. The measure seeks to restrict China and other US adversaries from accessing offshore computing power that uses American-designed processors. It comes as Wall Street awaits a price for the Anthropic IPO expected on Wednesday, with trading to begin Thursday on what could be the biggest first-time share sale ever.
On today’s episode:
Mike Shepard, Bloomberg News Senior Editor of Technology & Strategic Industries Ed Ludlow, Bloomberg Tech Host Bloomberg News Economics & Policy Correspondent Mike Mckee w/Beth Hammack, Cleveland Fed President Daniel Susskind, Author of ‘What Should My Children Do?: A Human’s Guide to the Age of AI’ (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Justice Department to Review DoorDash-Instacart Deal
item.description: The Justice Department will take the lead on reviewing DoorDash Inc.’s $17 billion Instacart purchase for potential antitrust concerns, according to US officials.
item.dc:creator: Leah Nylen

item.title: Xi-Trump-Putin Gets World Worrying About a Great Power Stitch-Up
item.description: At Yalta in 1945, the leaders of three dominant military powers gathered to craft a plan that would bring stability to the world – or conspired to carve it up among themselves.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Maryland Governor Moore on Midterms, FAA and AI Oversight
item.description: Maryland Governor Wes Moore says that what's "sorely missing" from the conversation about Friday's nationwide aviation shutdown is the "plan so this doesn't have to happen again," during an interview with Bloomberg's Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu. Moore also discusses the midterm elections, the potential government shutdown and the governance of AI data centers. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: New UK Relationship With Europe ‘Will Take Time,’ Burnham Says
item.description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham said any major change in the UK’s relationship with the Europe Union would “take time” and wouldn’t be implemented until after the next election in Britain.
item.dc:creator: Chloe Chaplain

item.title: Trump DOJ Willing to Clear More Merger Deals Without Asset Sales
item.description: The US Justice Department is open to approving mergers based on promises about how companies will operate rather than requiring them to sell assets, a senior official said Monday at a conference, pointing to the agency’s decision this month to clear Fox Corp.’s $22 billion acquisition of Roku Inc.
item.dc:creator: Georgia Fearn and Leah Nylen

item.title: Long-Awaited Milburn Report Calls for Tax Cuts, Tougher Welfare
item.description: To tackle its youth unemployment crisis the UK should cut taxes for businesses hiring young people while toughening the welfare system, a government-commissioned review into the problem will say.
item.dc:creator: Chloe Chaplain

item.title: Nvidia Fallout Raises Stakes for Trump-Xi Meeting
item.description: The US president’s moves could shape AI policies for years to come.
item.dc:creator: Alicia Diaz

item.title: US Moves to Curb China’s Chip Access
item.description: The Trump administration issued an interim rule requiring data center operators in several countries to obtain a US government license before exporting advanced AI chips from American manufacturers to customers in those countries. Bloomberg Senior Editor for Technology & Strategic Industries Michael Shepard explains the move. Then, Bloomberg’s Mike McKee interviews Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack on why she believes tighter rate policy moves are needed. Then, Bloomberg Law Immigration Reporter Andrew Kreighbaum explains the new Trump Administration proposal to righted rules for employer-sponsored green cards. Finally, Bank of America Head of Family Office Elizabeth Thiessen discusses the bank’s latest Family Office Study. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Maryland’s Moore Avoids 2028 Talk, Says Dems Must First Deliver
item.description: Maryland Governor Wes Moore, a Democrat who just won his second term, said voters in this month’s midterms sent an urgent message to their leaders that “we need you to start working right now to make our lives better.”
item.dc:creator: Catherine Lucey, Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu

item.title: Cleveland Fed's Hammack on Rate Policy, Inflation Targets, AI
item.description: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack says she enters each FOMC policy meeting with an open mind and says there is not much tension in their mandate to bring inflation down to 2%. She favors doing so in small and steady increments. She also speaks about AI, economic conditions and what she hears from business owners in her district. She speaks to Bloomberg's Michael McKee. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Backs Huang’s Return to Nvidia
item.description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz discuss the latest from DC. On today’s show, former Rep. Jane Harman (D-CA), Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino and Atmosphere Research Group President Henry Harteveldt. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Backs Huang Comeback While Nvidia Board Seeks New CEO
item.description: President Donald Trump supported calls from some Silicon Valley leaders for Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as Nvidia Corp.’s chief executive officer, despite the chipmaker’s board moving forward with its search for a new CEO.
item.dc:creator: Hadriana Lowenkron and Kate Sullivan
